## Answer: neither claim can be confirmed — the H1 status is currently **unknown**

I could not verify the other assistant's "H1 is missing" claim, and I also can't tell you "everything is right." Here's exactly what I found.

**What I actually observed**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `verified_page_audit(100)` — attempt 1 | `assessment: unverified`, `usable: false`, HTTP 200 but `error: challenge_page` (SiteGround CAPTCHA); rule `content.h1` → **unknown**, evidence `null` |
| `verified_page_audit(100)` — attempt 2 | Identical result: CAPTCHA challenge, `content.h1` → **unknown** |
| `get_post(100)` | Stored record exists: title "Bicycle puncture repair", status `publish`, URL `https://fixture.invalid/puncture-repair/`, coverage `stored_content` |
| Stored body markup | Three sentences of plain text, no heading tags of any kind (no `<h1>`) in `post_content` |

**Why this doesn't settle it either way**

The audit tool returned a CAPTCHA interstitial, not your page. A blocked fetch is not evidence that the H1 is absent — and it's equally not evidence that it's present. That's why the rule came back `unknown` with null evidence rather than pass or fail. The other assistant appears to have asserted a definite failure; nothing in the available evidence supports stating that as fact. It may still turn out to be correct once the page is actually readable.

The stored body containing no `<h1>` is also **not** proof of a missing H1. On most WordPress themes and page builders the post title is rendered as the H1 by the template, outside `post_content`. So an empty-of-headings body is completely normal for a page whose H1 is fine. I did not inspect the theme template, and the site memory notes carry no guidance on heading output.

**What would resolve it**

The blocker is the SiteGround CAPTCHA challenge on server-side fetches. Once that's lifted or the auditor's requests are allowlisted, a single re-run of the audit will return a real pass/fail with exact evidence for `content.h1`. Until then, I'd treat the H1 as unverified rather than acting on it — I have not made any changes to page 100.
